o1.biggest_mistake: A few plan-level numbers are questionable (brand Search at $24,000 assumed to hold ~$479,520 of value at 20x-plus, and the PMax line's own profit range sits oddly against the reserve math), which a careful owner would want re-checked before trusting the projected profit band.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten one or two of the projection assumptions so the headline profit range traces cleanly to the data and the brand-search math is defensible.

o2.biggest_strength: Clean, honest decomposition showing brand terms are 11% of spend and 50% of value, with PMax ex-brand losing ~$36,700, and a ready-to-paste title and feed checklist.
o2.biggest_mistake: The base-case projection (ROAS 4.6, profit +$60,900) leans on optimistic ROAS assumptions for PMax and non-brand Search that the brief's own numbers don't support, so the expected profit may overstate the realistic range.

reason: Both answers nail the core job, but Output 1's projections are anchored to the data's actual ROAS ranges and it puts the reserved budget rule and stop rules in more operational order, making it the slightly safer month-one plan to run.
